'''Gardens''' (or '''The Gardens''') is an affluent, predominantly [[residential]] suburb of [[Cape Town]], [[South Africa]]. It is located just to the south of the [[Cape Town CBD|CBD]], in the higher elevations of the [[City Bowl]] area, and directly beneath [[Table Mountain]] and [[Lion's Head (Cape Town)|Lion's Head]]. Gardens is home to several national [[museums]] such as [[Iziko South African National Gallery]] and the [[Iziko South African Museum]].

The [[University of Cape Town]] also houses its Fine Arts department in the suburb, at [[Michaelis School of Fine Art]]. [[Company's Garden]], South Africa's oldest garden, a public park and heritage site is a focal point of the suburb.  The area is also home to the oldest synagogue in Southern Africa, the '''Old Shul''' (now occupied by the [[South African Jewish Museum]]) and its successor, the [[Gardens Shul]], "The Mother Synagogue of South Africa." 

It is also home to the storied [[Belmond Mount Nelson Hotel]], a luxury hotel dating back to 1899,<ref>[https://www.nytimes.com/1979/01/20/archives/south-africans-cling-to-a-lovely-old-city-the-talk-of-cape-town.html South Africans Cling to a Lovely Old City] ''The New York Times''. 20 January 1979</ref> as well as the [[Labia Theatre]], a beloved independent [[art house]] cinema.<ref>[https://www.theguardian.com/world/2014/jul/24/south-africa-labia-cape-town Curtains? Cape Town's much-loved art house cinema under threat] ''The Guardian''. 24 July 2014</ref> The main thoroughfare is '''Kloof Street''', known for its fashion stores, second-hand furniture stores, restaurants and art galleries.<ref>[https://www.timeout.com/things-to-do/coolest-streets-in-the-world The 33 coolest streets in the world] ''TimeOut''. 25 August 2022</ref> It also houses [[Leeuwenhof]] estate, the [[official residence]] of the [[Premier of the Western Cape]]. It is a hub for the [[Cape Town]] creative industry, home to [[e.tv]] at Longkloof Studios and many modelling agencies, production and publishing companies and associated industries.

==History==
In the early years, the Cape was used as an anchorage for Portuguese, Dutch and British ships.
No permanent settlement existed until the [[Dutch East India Company]] issued a mandate to [[Jan van Riebeeck]], a ship's surgeon, to establish a settlement which could provide passing ships with fruit, vegetables and fresh meat (traded from the locals).

In 1652 the first garden was laid out by Hendrik Boom, the Company's master gardener, on a site close to the Fresh River (near to the Grand Parade). Later that year, the garden crossed the Fresh River (where [[Adderley Street]] is today), and included a medicine garden. Within a few years it was 18 hectares in size.

As more produce became available from  the Company's gardens at [[Newlands, Cape Town|Newlands]] and from the [[Free Burghers]] who had settled along the [[Liesbeeck River]], the town garden was slowly converted into a botanical and ornamental garden, although the growing of vegetables did continue for a number of years.

The famous kilometre-long Government Avenue, which runs from the top of [[Adderley Street]], also known as 'The Gardens', was originally planted with lemon trees and in 1700 with orange trees. During the time of [[Simon van der Stel]], it was lined with oak trees, which remain today.

The suburb is home to Southern Africa's oldest Jewish congregation. The first Jewish services in the country were held on the day preceding [[Yom Kippur]] in 1841, known as '''Erev Yom Kippur''' at Benjamin Norden's home, Helmsley Place. The [[Belmond Mount Nelson Hotel]] purchased Norden's former home in 1996 and it is now guest accommodation for the hotel.<ref>[https://www.belmond.com/ideas/articles/belmond-mount-nelson-hotel-history Mount Nelson, A Belmond Hotel, Cape Town: A Timeline] Belmond. Accessed on 12.9.23</ref><ref name=for/>

In the early twentieth century, a Jewish primary school was established on Hope Street, '''United Hebrew Schools''''.  A purpose-built school was built at the same site in 1937, replacing the large house that had previously housed the school.<ref>[https://open.uct.ac.za/handle/11427/23668 The history of Jewish education in South Africa, 1841-1980 (part 1)] University of Cape Town. 1980</ref> The school later became known as [[United Herzlia Schools|Herzlia School]] and relocated to its current campus in [[Vredehoek]] in the 1950s, where a high school was also established.<ref>[https://open.uct.ac.za/handle/11427/23668 The history of Jewish education in South Africa, 1841-1980 (part 2)] University of Cape Town. 1980</ref>

During [[apartheid]], Vredehoek was designated as a “whites-only” area as part of the [[Group Areas Act]]. The Gardens Centre Tower was built in the 1970s in response to a "[[white South African|white]] housing crisis" in racially segregated Cape Town. In the 1970s the [[National Party (South Africa)|National Party]] initiated several planning interventions, including the suspension of the city's zoning rules with regards to building height for developers willing to build housing in white [[Group Areas Act|Group Areas]].<ref>[https://visi.co.za/building-an-icon-disa-park/ Building an icon: Disi Park] Visi. 13 March 2023</ref>

The residential tower and shopping mall replaced a large historic hotel, '''The International Hotel''' situated on Upper Mill Street. The [[South Africa national rugby union team]] (Springboks) usually stayed there when they were playing in Cape Town. The hotel also hosted bands and concerts over the weekends.<ref>[https://www.vryeweekblad.com/en/opinions-and-debate/2024-03-08-ugly-as-a-wet-mop-intriguing-as-a-snake/ Ugly as a wet mop, intriguing as a snake] ''Vrye Weekblad''. 8 March 2024</ref>

Kloof Street mostly consisted of boarding houses for most of the twentieth century, many have now been converted into restaurants, cafes, boutiques and hotels.<ref>{{cite book

== Places of interest ==
* [[Belmond Mount Nelson Hotel]], one of the oldest and most historic hotels in all of Africa
* [[Leeuwenhof]], the official residence of the [[Premier of the Western Cape]]
* [[Labia Theatre]], one of the oldest independent movie theatres in the city 

===Parks===
*[[Company's Garden]], the oldest garden in South Africa, a public park and heritage site. 
*[[De Waal Park]] is a public park and heritage site in the neighbouring suburb of [[Oranjezicht]]

===Museums===
* [[Iziko South African National Gallery]], the national art gallery of South Africa 
* [[Iziko South African Museum]], the oldest in the country, was established in 1825 and houses important African [[zoology]], [[palaeontology]] and [[archaeology]] collections. It also contains a planetarium. 
* The [[South African Jewish Museum]], opened in 2000, and housed in purpose-built modern buildings and in the original synagogue, known as 'The [[Gardens Shul]]', the [[Oldest synagogues in the World|oldest Jewish congregation]] in Southern Africa built in 1862. It is known as the “mother synagogue” of South Africa.<ref name=for>[https://forward.com/news/175662/cape-towns-jewish-history-on-display/ Cape Town’s Jewish History on Display] Forward. 29 April 2013</ref> The twin-towered 'new' synagogue was built in 1905. Gardens, [[Vredehoek]] and [[Sea Point]] have traditionally attracted Jewish communities.<ref name=tab>[https://www.tabletmag.com/sections/community/articles/jewish-south-africa-rainbow-nation The Future of Jewish South Africa] Tablet Mag. 22 March 2023</ref>
* [[Cape Town Holocaust Centre]], Africa's first [[Holocaust]] centre, founded in 1999

==Houses of worship==
[[File:Company Gardens. Great Synagogue seen from Paddocks.jpg|thumb|Gardens Shul]]
*[[Gardens Shul]], an [[Orthodox Jewish]] synagogue located in the historic [[Company Gardens (Cape Town)|Company Gardens]]
*St. Barnabas Church, [[Anglican]] church on Kloof Nek Road & Kamp Street 
*Cape Peninsula Reformed Church, English-speaking congregation of the [[Dutch Reformed Church in South Africa (NGK)]] on Kloof Street
*Gereformeerde Kerk Kaapstad, [[Reformed Churches in South Africa|Reformed]] church on Hof St
*The Union Chapel, [[Presbyterian]] church on corner of Kloof Street & Eaton Road
* Father's House Church, [[Assemblies of God]] church on Vrede Street 
*Jubilee Community Church, located on Kloof Street
*New Life City Church Cape Town, [[Evangelical]] church on Kloof Street

==Education==
[[File:Hoërskool Jan van Riebeeck, Cape Town.jpg|thumb|Hoërskool Jan van Riebeeck, Cape Town]]
===Schools===
====Public====
* [[Cape Town High School]], an [[English language|English medium]] co-educational high school 
* [[Good Hope Seminary High School]], an English medium all-girls high school founded in 1873 by Reverend Andrew Murray
* [[Gardens Commercial High School]], an English-medium co-educational high school 
* St Mary's Primary School, an English medium co-educational [[Catholic]] primary school 
* [[Hoërskool Jan van Riebeeck]], an [[Afrikaans language|Afrikaans medium]] high school<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.janvanriebeeck.co.za/ |title=Hoërskool Jan van Riebeeck | Wees Uself |publisher=Janvanriebeeck.co.za |date= |accessdate=2022-04-11}}</ref>
* Jan Van Riebeeck Primary School, an Afrikaans medium primary school<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.jvrprim.co.za |title=Laerskool Jan van Riebeeck | Wees Uself |publisher=Jvrprim.co.za |date= |accessdate=2022-04-11}}</ref>

====Private====

[[Cape Town French School]]. Retrieved on 22 January 2015. "Lycée Français du Cap 101, Hope Street - Gardens 8001 Cape Town South Africa" and "Ecole Française du Cap Corner Tramway and Kings road - Sea Point 8005 Cape Town South Africa"</ref>
* [[St. Cyprian's School, Cape Town|St. Cyprian's School]], an all-girls [[Anglican]] pre-primary, primary and high school in neighbourhing [[Oranjezicht]]<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.stcyprians.co.za/ |title=St Cyprian's | Girls School | Cape Town |publisher=Stcyprians.co.za |date= |accessdate=2022-04-11}}</ref>

===Higher education===
* [[Michaelis School of Fine Art]], Fine Arts department of the [[University of Cape Town]], founded in 1925 and named after its benefactor, [[Max Michaelis]]
* [[CityVarsity]], a school of media and creative arts on Roeland St.

===Libraries===
*Kloof Street Public Library, at 122B Kloof Street
*[[Jacob Gitlin Library]], a Jewish library and archive of information on [[Judaism]], [[Jewish culture]] and history, and the nation of [[Israel]]

==Transportation==
The suburb is served by the MyCiTi [[bus rapid transit]] system. The 101 route takes passengers to [[Vredehoek]] and the [[Cape Town Civic Centre]] in central Cape Town. The 113 route takes passengers to [[Adderley Street]] and the [[V&A Waterfront]]. The 107 route goes to [[Camps Bay]].<ref>[https://www.myciti.org.za/docs/categories/3551/BRANDED_SYSTEM_MAP_DECEMBER_2022.pdf MyCiTi System Map] Accessed on 12.9.2023</ref>

==In popular culture==
*''[[Age of Iron]]'', a 1990 novel by [[J. M. Coetzee]] takes places in and around the suburb. The elderly white protagonist, Mrs. Curren lives in a home situated in the area of Breda Street, Schoonder Street and Vrede Street.<ref>[https://repozytorium.uwb.edu.pl/jspui/bitstream/11320/13786/1/Crossroads_36_2022_K_Jeczminska_Spiritual_and_material_dimensions_of_home.pdf Spiritual and material dimensions of home in J. M.Coetzee’s Age of Iron] Jagiellonian University. 2022</ref>
*Mabu Viny, a record store, previously on 2 Rheede St, features prominently in the documentary, ''[[Searching for Sugar Man]]''<ref>[https://thevinylfactory.com/features/the-worlds-best-record-shops-020-mabu-vinyl-cape-town/ The world’s best record shops #020: Mabu Vinyl, Cape Town] ''The Vinyl Factory''. 19 May 2016</ref>
